content.text: I read all three input files, the numeral ledger, all seven figure briefs, and every draft section, then traced each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement back to the disclosure.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and dependents 2-12, 14-17, 19-22), all 27 entries in draft/numerals.md, all seven figure briefs, the Brief Description of the Drawings, the Summary, Detailed Description, and Abstract were checked line by line against the affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md (input/conversation.md is a truncated duplicate of the same USER text; input/brief.md was used only for the no-priority, no-government-support, apparatus-plus-method, no-means-plus-function, and preserved-terminology formalities). Every technical assertion traced to an exact affirmative source passage: rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot and printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end with a downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge, perpendicular to the rail; reversibility by removing two screws received in two corresponding holes, inverting, and reinstalling so the projecting part moves to the opposite longitudinal side while the same marked upper face is used; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate guide carriages with anti-rotation keys in the slot, one cylindrical hardened-metal replaceable drill bushing each with a vertical bore passing completely through the carriage and registering with the slot, the two bore axes parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail with a shank through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail that clamps the rail between carriage and shoe; per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and read against the same distance marks with the difference being center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index and with the pencil centerline; the full use sequence; the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list; and the no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection limitation. No untraced structure, relationship, result, material, shape, position, connection, operating condition, or variant was found, so there is no critical disclosure_fidelity finding: the dependent-claim limitations (uncoupled bodies, same-scale reading difference, same reading direction after reversal, withdrawable hardened bushings, shoe bearing on the lower face, hand-held operation, perpendicular holes) each rest on an affirmative disclosure sentence, and the schematic block, rectangle, round-knob, graduation-line, index-line, and page-placement statements in the briefs are confined to the briefs, are called "shown schematically", add no undisclosed proportion, count, taper, depth, runout, or contact topology, and are not verbalized in the application text (no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language appears anywhere). Numerals are one-to-one with parts, every ledger numeral appears in at least one brief, no brief uses a numeral outside the ledger, and the section-line designations are consistent across FIG. 2 (line 3-3 across the second guide carriage 70, line 5-5 across the first guide carriage 50), the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 headings, and the Brief Description. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains, claim dependencies are all backward and supported by description hooks, and the abstract is 149 words. Three verified internal-consistency defects remain, all in the drawing-to-text interface: the description cites FIG. 1 for numeral 32 that FIG. 1 does not label; the FIG. 2 brief defines both cutting planes by the drill bushing bore axis and the clamp knob axis while omitting those features from the view and its numeral list even though FIG. 1 shows the knobs standing above the carriages; and no figure brief states the sight notch 26 / transverse center index 24 alignment that claims 5, 13, and 18 recite. Each is reported with a filing-clean fix that adds only source-supported wording.

findings.title: Description cites FIG. 1 for reference numeral 32, which FIG. 1 does not label
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, fence paragraph; figures/FIG-1.md (body and "Numerals shown on this figure")
findings.detail: The detailed description directs the reader to FIG. 1 for the downwardly projecting portion 32, but the FIG. 1 brief describes that feature only in unnumbered words ("A part of the fence 30 depends alongside the longitudinal side of the rail 10 ... and contacts the workpiece edge 92") and its numeral list contains only 10, 30, 50, 58, 70, 78, 90, 92. The numeral 32 is labeled only in FIG. 4 and FIG. 6, so the FIG. 1 cross-reference points to a numeral that does not appear in that view. The underlying structure is source-supported ("The fence extends downward from the lower face and bears against one straight edge of the workpiece"; "moves the downwardly projecting part of the fence from one longitudinal side of the rail to the opposite longitudinal side"), so this is a labeling defect rather than a fidelity defect.
findings.evidence: Description: "As seen in FIG. 1, the downwardly projecting portion 32 bears against the workpiece edge 92." FIG-1.md numeral list: "- 10: rail / - 30: fence / - 50: first guide carriage / - 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage / - 70: second guide carriage / - 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage / - 90: workpiece / - 92: workpiece edge" (no 32).
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change the sentence to "A downwardly projecting portion 32 of the fence 30 depends alongside the longitudinal side of the rail 10 that faces the workpiece edge 92, extends below the rail 10, and contacts the workpiece edge 92," and add "- 32: downwardly projecting portion" to the FIG. 1 numeral list, matching the wording already used in figures/FIG-4.md and figures/FIG-6.md. Leave the description sentence unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 2 locates both cutting planes on the bushing bore and clamp knob axes but omits those features from the view
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, cutting-plane paragraphs and "Numerals shown on this figure"
findings.detail: The FIG. 2 brief places each stepped cutting plane by reference to "the axis of the drill bushing bore of that carriage" and "the axis of its clamp knob," yet the same brief renders each carriage as a bare "plain rectangular body" and lists no numeral for the drill bushings 54, 74 or the clamp knobs 58, 78. FIG. 1 shows a clamp knob standing above each carriage, so a top plan view of the same jig must show them; as written, FIG. 2 defines its section lines by features it does not depict or label, and a reader cannot verify that line 3-3 and line 5-5 are correctly placed. Both features are affirmatively disclosed ("Each carriage carries one cylindrical drill bushing with a vertical bore"; "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail"), so adding them introduces no new matter.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "Each carriage overlaps and hides the part of the longitudinal slot 16 beneath it." and "one transverse leg lying on the axis of the drill bushing bore of that carriage and the other on the axis of its clamp knob"; numeral list: "- 10 / - 16 / - 18 / - 30 / - 50 / - 62 / - 70 / - 82" (no 54, 58, 74, 78).
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, after the paragraph introducing the two carriages add: "The clamp knob 58 of the first guide carriage 50 and the clamp knob 78 of the second guide carriage 70 are seen from above on their respective carriages, and the bore of the drill bushing 54 of the first guide carriage 50 and the bore of the drill bushing 74 of the second guide carriage 70 open through the top of their respective carriages." Add "- 54: drill bushing of the first guide carriage", "- 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage", "- 74: drill bushing of the second guide carriage", and "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage" to the FIG. 2 numeral list.

findings.title: No figure brief depicts the claimed alignment of the sight notch 26 with the transverse center index 24
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md; draft/09-claims.md claims 5, 13, 18; draft/08-detailed-description.md, centering paragraph
findings.detail: The alignment of the sight notch with the transverse center index is a recited claim limitation and a described relationship, but FIG. 7 — the only view containing both features — describes each independently and never states that they are aligned. The brief instead fixes the centerline 94 as running "transverse to the length of the rail 10 in line with the transverse center index 24" while placing the transverse center index 24 "in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end of the rail 10" where the notch is, so the drawing as briefed shows the centerline registering with the index alone and leaves the claimed notch-to-index alignment undepicted. The relationship is verbatim in the source, so stating it in the brief adds nothing beyond the disclosure.
findings.evidence: Claim 5: "a shallow V-shaped sight notch formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the transverse center index"; description: "A shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 (FIG. 7) is formed in the second end of the rail 10 and is aligned with the transverse center index 24"; disclosure: "A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index." FIG-7.md says only: "A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10, shown schematically."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace that sentence with: "A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10 and aligned with the transverse center index 24, shown schematically." Make no change to the claims or the detailed description, and add no further geometry to the brief.
